node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Describe translations
node.description: Describe a slide of a shape or object using direction and distance language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Describe reflections
node.description: Describe a flip of a shape or object across a mirror line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Describe rotations
node.description: Describe a turn of a shape or object around a centre point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Before and after figures
node.description: Compare a figure before and after a transformation to describe what changed and what stayed the same.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Image and preimage language
node.description: Use image and preimage language for a figure before and after a transformation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compose simple transformations
node.description: Apply two or more simple transformations in sequence and describe the result.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Line symmetry
node.description: Identify whether a figure has a line that divides it into matching mirror-image halves.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Draw lines of symmetry
node.description: Draw all lines of symmetry for common shapes and designs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reflection symmetry in shapes
node.description: Connect reflection symmetry to a shape matching itself across a symmetry line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rotational symmetry
node.description: Identify when a shape matches itself after a turn less than a full turn.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Symmetry in designs
node.description: Identify line and rotational symmetry in patterns, designs and visual contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate symmetry
node.description: Describe symmetry of figures using axes and coordinates in the coordinate plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Transformations on grids
node.description: Represent translations, reflections and rotations of figures on square grids.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate translations
node.description: Use coordinate changes to represent translations in the coordinate plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate reflections over axes
node.description: Reflect points and figures over the coordinate axes and describe coordinate changes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate rotations by quarter turns
node.description: Rotate points and figures by quarter turns around the origin and describe coordinate changes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate dilations
node.description: Represent dilations in the coordinate plane using scale factors.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Transformation rules
node.description: Use rules to describe how coordinates change under transformations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rigid transformations and congruence
node.description: Recognise that translations, reflections and rotations preserve size and shape.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dilations and similarity
node.description: Recognise that dilations preserve shape while changing size by a scale factor.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sequence coordinate transformations
node.description: Apply and describe sequences of transformations in the coordinate plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Translation preserves orientation
node.description: A translation slides every point the same distance and direction without turning or flipping the figure.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reflection uses a mirror line
node.description: A reflection maps points to mirror positions across a reflection line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rotation uses centre angle and direction
node.description: A rotation is described by a centre, angle and direction of turn.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Image follows preimage
node.description: The image is the result of transforming the original preimage.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Line symmetry maps figure to itself
node.description: A line of symmetry maps a figure onto itself by reflection.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rotational symmetry repeats after a turn
node.description: A figure has rotational symmetry when it matches itself after a turn less than a full turn.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rigid transformations preserve size and shape
node.description: Translations, reflections and rotations preserve side lengths and angle measures.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dilations scale distances
node.description: A dilation multiplies distances from a centre by a scale factor.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinates track movement
node.description: Coordinate changes can describe the movement of points under transformations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Transformation order can matter
node.description: Applying transformations in a different order can produce a different final image.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reflection treated as translation
node.description: Learner slides a figure instead of reflecting it across a mirror line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rotation around wrong centre
node.description: Learner rotates a figure around an unintended centre point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Translation changes size
node.description: Learner changes the size or shape of a figure while translating it.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Any centre line is symmetry
node.description: Learner assumes any line through the centre of a figure is a line of symmetry.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dilation treated as addition
node.description: Learner treats dilation as adding a fixed amount to coordinates or lengths rather than multiplying by a scale factor.

edge.rationale: Translations are the formal version of slides in this transformation progression.
Reflections are the formal version of flips in this transformation progression.
Rotations are the formal version of turns in this transformation progression.
Before-and-after comparison supports recognising transformation effects.
Image and preimage language supports formal transformation descriptions.
Composing simple transformations extends basic transformation actions.
Line symmetry is a central form of symmetry in shapes and designs.
Drawing symmetry lines directly practises identifying line symmetry.
Reflection symmetry connects symmetry to a transformation idea.
Rotational symmetry is a key extension of symmetry beyond mirror lines.
Design contexts apply line and rotational symmetry recognition.
Coordinate symmetry extends symmetry into coordinate representations.
Grid transformations bridge informal transformations and coordinate transformations.
Translations are a central coordinate transformation.
Reflections over axes are central coordinate transformations.
Quarter-turn rotations are common coordinate transformations.
Dilations extend coordinate transformations to scaling and similarity.
Transformation rules describe coordinate changes formally.
Rigid transformations connect coordinate transformation work to congruence.
Dilations connect coordinate transformations to similarity.
Transformation sequences extend single-coordinate transformation rules.
Translations use direction and distance language from early position work.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot describe the direction or distance of a slide.

edge.rationale: Reflection work requires recognising a figure across changed orientation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats the reflected figure as unrelated rather than mirrored.

edge.rationale: Rotation descriptions use the idea of a turn through an angle around a centre.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot distinguish a turn from a slide or flip.

edge.rationale: Before-and-after transformation comparisons build from recognising simple slides, flips and turns.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify what transformation changed the figure.

edge.rationale: Image and preimage language formalises before-and-after transformation comparison.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify original and transformed figures.

edge.rationale: Composing transformations requires tracking successive images from a preimage.
edge.failure_signal: Learner loses track of the intermediate image in a transformation sequence.

edge.rationale: Line symmetry is based on a figure matching itself under reflection.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies visual balance without a valid mirror line.

edge.rationale: Drawing symmetry lines requires recognising where a figure reflects onto itself.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws lines that do not create matching halves.

edge.rationale: Reflection symmetry in shapes builds directly on line-symmetry recognition.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect symmetry to a reflection across a line.

edge.rationale: Rotational symmetry depends on understanding a turn around a centre.
edge.failure_signal: Learner only checks mirror lines and misses rotational matches.

edge.rationale: Symmetry in designs applies line and rotational symmetry recognition in visual contexts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies decorative repetition but not the symmetry relationship.

edge.rationale: Coordinate symmetry requires using axes and coordinate locations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot describe symmetry using coordinates or axes.

edge.rationale: Grid transformations require following locations and movements on grids.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot track the transformed figure across grid positions.

edge.rationale: Coordinate translations depend on locating and moving points in the coordinate plane.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot express a slide as changes in x and y coordinates.

edge.rationale: Coordinate reflections build on tracking coordinates before and after transformations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes both coordinates incorrectly when reflecting over an axis.

edge.rationale: Coordinate rotations require more complex coordinate-change reasoning than axis reflections.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies a reflection rule when a rotation rule is needed.

edge.rationale: Coordinate dilations use scale factors and proportional distance changes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner adds fixed amounts rather than multiplying by a scale factor.

edge.rationale: Transformation rules formalise coordinate transformations as coordinate-change patterns.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes movement visually but cannot express it as a rule.

edge.rationale: Rigid transformation congruence builds from coordinate translations and reflections that preserve size and shape.
edge.failure_signal: Learner thinks a moved or reflected figure is no longer congruent.

edge.rationale: Similarity through transformations requires understanding dilation as scaling.
edge.failure_signal: Learner recognises same shape visually but cannot connect it to a scale factor.

edge.rationale: Transformation sequences require applying coordinate transformation rules in order.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies rules in the wrong order or loses track of intermediate images.
